## TL;DR

Updated the Checks page header for phone widths. The page now presents a compact purpose line beneath the heading, followed by full-width Help and Edit plan actions with 42px minimum height. Desktop keeps its existing detailed descriptions and action labels. The tab bar remains in normal page flow below the header.

## Work and rationale

The page had a tab-dependent description that was useful on desktop but lengthy at narrow widths. A shared style rule also hid `.ck-sub` entirely on mobile. The change keeps that full description in a desktop-only span and adds a short mobile sentence for each active tab: the plan, test suite, recent runs, or currently running and waiting checks. That gives users a useful orientation without allowing the explanatory paragraph to dominate the first screen.

The actions previously shared a right-side flex area in the header. At phone widths the header now stacks its title and actions vertically. Help and Edit plan use a two-column grid that takes the available width, with centered labels, visible borders and a 42px minimum target height. Short mobile labels avoid wrapping at 320px, while the original labels remain visible at desktop widths. The refresh action is still available on the plan tab and can wrap naturally as part of the action row.

No check behavior or routing changed. The tab navigation stays directly after the header, so it remains reachable and follows the same content order on desktop and mobile. The layout uses existing theme tokens for borders and text, so the controls follow the active light or dark theme.

## Approaches tried

I first considered simply un-hiding the current subtitle on mobile. That would restore useful context but would preserve several lines of copy, the original issue at 390px. The final approach retains the desktop copy and provides separate concise mobile text instead. I also considered leaving actions as inline links; a full-width two-column action row makes their tap area predictable and removes the narrow side column.

The checked-in shot declarations cover the default Runs view and a populated history fixture. The implementation is responsive CSS and conditional text; there is no state-specific behavior beyond the currently selected tab.

## Challenges and blockers

The page-specific subtitle was included in a shared mobile rule that hides explanatory subtitles on other views. The view-scoped mobile rule now intentionally restores `.ck-sub` only for Checks, while hiding the longer content span there. This keeps the existing shared behavior intact for other pages.

I did not claim a physical-device inspection or a manual visual comparison in both themes. The required scoped RepoOS check is the verification gate for this handoff; any visual capture produced by RepoOS can be used in review. No human-only requirement was found in the implementation.

## Key learnings

Responsive page headers can preserve useful desktop explanations without forcing them onto small screens. A concise, tab-aware summary keeps context relevant, and moving actions into a full-width row gives both links room for comfortable targets. Scoped overrides are important when a page-specific subtitle participates in shared clutter-reduction styles.
